mappings.note: Reads an account of a Russian wedding and sorts its customs into those like Indian ones and those unlike them - exactly the comparison LO-10 names.
'Find reason for your answer from the play' makes textual evidence the marked skill, LO-3; LO-2 would cover only the verdict on Chubukov's sincerity.
A character sketch of Natalya. LO-2 covers character analysis; no evidence is demanded, so not LO-3.
'Justify the statement' about the land-grabber jibe requires the exchange from the play as support - evidence, LO-3.
His evening dress and his purpose are both stated in the opening scene; retrieval, LO-1.
'How can you say' requires the learner to quote Natalya's own claim about three hundred years of ownership - evidence, LO-3.
The palpitations and the sleeplessness are stated in Lomov's speeches; retrieval, LO-1.
The request for Natalya's hand is stated; retrieval, LO-1.
Asks what a quoted line conveys about Chubukov as a father - character analysis, LO-2.
A speech draft on relationships across two texts, with set opening and closing lines. Structured composition, C-E1.2; it is not about wedding customs (LO-10) or marrying for property (LO-11).
Look up three idiomatic phrases and use each in a sentence. Phrase meaning and usage, C-E1.1.
States the tense rule for reported speech when the reporting verb is present. A grammatical convention, C-E1.3. (Its stored answer belongs to a different item.)
Part i asks the learner to collect the actual insults from the play (evidence, LO-3); part ii turns them into five adjectives for each character (LO-2).
Contrasts translated Russian forms of address with idiomatic modern English in the same play. Register and expression, C-E1.1, not a wedding-custom comparison.
Dictionary work on pronunciation, syllable count and stress for a list of words from the play. Word study, C-E1.1; the row's stored answer has been crossed with an unrelated passage.
A group discussion recounting comparable scenes from romantic comedies. Spoken expression of the learner's own examples, C-E1.2.
Chubukov's suspicion that Lomov wants a loan is stated; retrieval, LO-1.
The purpose of the evening dress is stated; retrieval, LO-1.
'Lovesick cat' is Chubukov's phrase for Natalya, said aloud in the play; retrieval, LO-1.
His three reasons - his age, his palpitations, his broken sleep - are all listed in his own speech; retrieval, LO-1.
The quarrel starts over Oxen Meadows, as the text shows; retrieval, LO-1.
Lomov's claim about his aunt's grandmother and the peasants is stated; retrieval, LO-1.
The MCQ's options are the errands the play makes him run, so the answer is retrieved, LO-1, while the 'what does the line convey about him' version is the LO-2 item.
Authorship of the play. Knowledge about the work itself, which no LO covers.
The moment of acceptance - when Lomov faints - is a stage event; retrieval, LO-1.
Shelling peas is stated in her entrance line; retrieval, LO-1.
Guess is named in the text; retrieval, LO-1.
The twenty-five roubles figure is stated; retrieval, LO-1.
The inheritance from his aunt and uncle is stated; retrieval, LO-1.
The elopement with an architect is one of the insults thrown in the quarrel and is stated outright; retrieval, LO-1.
The lent threshing machine is stated; retrieval, LO-1.
Oxen Meadows as the first subject of the quarrel is stated; retrieval, LO-1.
Squeezer is named in the text; retrieval, LO-1.
The jibe about the humpbacked mother is spoken in the play; retrieval, LO-1.
Asks what the formal clothes signal about Lomov's purpose and feelings - an inference about the character, LO-2, since the play never says he loves her.
Why Chubukov is delighted - he wants his daughter married off - is his motive as a character, LO-2.

Identifies the practical, unromantic view of marriage all three characters hold - the writer's point about them, LO-2. It asks for a judgement about the play, not the learner's own opinion, so not LO-11.
His two stated considerations - his age and his need for a settled life - come straight from his speech; retrieval, LO-1.
The purpose of his visit is stated; retrieval, LO-1.
Duplicate of the visit-purpose item; a stated fact, LO-1.
